hero.title: EcoRisk — Environmental Risk Platform
hero.context: Turned risk into safe decision-making for environmental credit approval.
hero.note: Client and product names in this case study have been anonymized to “EcoRisk” in line with the confidentiality terms of this project. [Confidential detail omitted where the source material did not specify timeline, team size, or scope.]

challenge.heading: Challenge / problem
paragraphs: Incomplete and disorganized information, along with usability and accessibility issues, created a risk of misinterpretation.
Two consequences stood out: inconsistency — divergent analyses for the same client — and omission — vital data ignored in reports.
The problem wasn’t a lack of information, it was disorganization.

costOfUncertainty.title: Rework
costOfUncertainty.desc: lack of confidence in preliminary analyses

costOfUncertainty.title: Losses
costOfUncertainty.desc: financial losses due to improper approvals

process.heading: Process
process.intro: Before the screen, I organized decisions.

pillars.title: Identification
pillars.desc: visualization of property boundaries on the map

process.validation: I validated with the users before writing any code. Early alignment ensured full adoption of the solution.

journey.heading: Journey simplification
journey.summary: Reduction from 7~9 steps to 4, ensuring the credit analyst follows the regulatory journey without deviations.
after: Starts the search by CAR number, CPF/CNPJ, map click, or coordinates
The system automatically cross-references all compliance rules
Views consolidated risks directly on the property map
Moves on to the next step of the credit analysis
legend: Time reduced by 60s or more per step

items.title: Decision-oriented interface
items.desc: Search expanded to 3 new parameters, giving flexibility in data input and reducing friction and complexity.
items.alt: EcoRisk search panel with options to search by CAR number, CPF/CNPJ, map click, or coordinates, alongside a satellite map of Brazil.
items.caption: The consultation panel consolidates every search method — CAR number, document number, map click, or coordinates — into one interface.

items.title: Highlight for the selected area
items.desc: Selecting a property directly on the map highlights the chosen polygon, reducing uncertainty and preventing errors.
items.alt: Satellite map showing multiple highlighted yellow property boundaries, with one boundary outlined in teal to indicate the selected polygon.
items.caption: Clicking a polygon on the map highlights the selected property boundary among overlapping records.

items.title: Institution management
items.desc: The regulatory institution manages the registry of financial institutions, supporting security, efficiency, and transparency.
items.alt: Institution management table listing financial institutions with banking codes, domains, and options to edit or block each entry.
items.caption: An administrative view lets the regulator manage which financial institutions can access the platform.

items.title: Exportable risk report
items.desc: The platform generates a documented, exportable report cross-referencing every relevant compliance layer for a given property.
items.alt: First page of an EcoRisk environmental risk report, showing property owner information, cadastral situation, and a satellite map of the property boundary.
items.caption: Report cover page with property identification, cadastral status, and a satellite view of the property boundary.

items.title: Spatial overlap conformity
items.desc: Each relevant regulatory layer is cross-referenced automatically and shown with a clear conformity indicator.
items.alt: Table of spatial overlap information listing regulatory layers such as embargoes, indigenous lands, and conservation units, each with a conformity status icon.
items.caption: Every regulatory layer — embargoes, indigenous lands, conservation units, and more — is checked automatically and flagged with a conformity status.

outcomes.heading: Outcomes and learnings

speed.label: Before
speed.value: Reports generated with a high risk of human error

speed.label: After
speed.value: -2 minutes to generate complete reports (100+ pages). Searches in under 60s.

businessImpact.label: in fines received for improper credit approval
new timeframe for the approval process (previously a minimum of 3 weeks)

outcomes.closing: What matters: trust. More than just pretty screens, this delivered standardized decisions and reliable data. Risk was mitigated through process design.
summary: The routine required cross-referencing dispersed data to validate a scenario.
The interface took on the role of connecting this information and guiding data reading.
The delivered model reduced manual effort and made the process predictable.
